questions: What is the exact condition for the game to end - when S becomes empty or when no moves are possible?
Is the initial set S empty at the start of the game or does it contain some elements?
What happens if multiple indices have the same value when choosing which index to decrement?
Does the game end immediately when S becomes empty or after the current player completes their turn?
Are the players allowed to choose any valid index or must they follow a specific strategy beyond optimal play?
What is the precise definition of "playing optimally" in this context - maximizing own moves or minimizing opponent's advantage?
Is there a time limit or move limit for the game, or does it continue until the mathematical end condition is met?
How should ties or draws be handled if they are possible under the given rules?
answers: The game ends when S becomes {1,2,...,N} (the full set), not when S is empty.
Yes, S is initially empty, as explicitly stated.
Not applicable; a player may freely choose among any valid indices.
The game ends immediately once S becomes {1,2,...,N}, right after the operation that completes it.
Players may choose any valid index (A_i ≥ 1); 'optimal play' just means choosing the strategically best such index.
Both players play deterministically to guarantee a win whenever one is achievable for them.
There's no artificial time or move limit; the game continues until S = {1,2,...,N} is reached.
Since the game is guaranteed to terminate with a winner, a draw cannot occur.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that A_i. Subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. - If S=\{1,2,\dots,N\}, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
